chapters.summary: Paul urges the Corinthian believers to be united in Christ and avoid divisions, and points out that the wisdom of God far exceeds the wisdom of man.
keyPoints: Paul greets the church and gives thanks to God, because in Christ the Corinthians have been enriched in every way, in all utterance and all knowledge.
Paul urges the believers to be of the same mind and judgment, and not to split into factions, for Christ is not divided.
Paul stresses that the preaching of the cross is the power of God, and that the wisdom of God surpasses the wisdom of man.
chapters.application: In the church, let us keep Christ at the center and pursue unity, boasting not in human wisdom but only in the Lord. May we humbly receive the salvation of the cross and live out the life of Christ.

chapters.summary: Paul explains that he did not preach with lofty words or human wisdom, but relied on the demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that the believers' faith would rest on the power of God, and he teaches that only the spiritual man can understand the deep things of God.
keyPoints: When Paul preached at Corinth, he did not come with excellency of speech or of wisdom, but determined to know nothing among them except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
The believers' faith does not rest on human wisdom but on the power of God, confirmed by the demonstration of the Spirit and of power.
The spiritual man can discern all things, for the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
chapters.application: Let us humbly depend on the Holy Spirit rather than on human cleverness, seeking God's will in faith and in life, and experiencing his power.

chapters.summary: Paul points out that the Corinthians are still carnal, as shown by their envy and strife, and stresses that the church is God's field and God's building, with Jesus Christ as its foundation.
keyPoints: Paul rebukes the believers for still being carnal, dividing into factions after the manner of men.
He explains that those who preach are only servants, and it is God who gives the increase.
He warns that everyone must take care how they build, for the foundation is Christ.
chapters.application: Let us examine whether we often act according to the flesh, pursue peace and unity, and remember that Christ alone is the foundation - for everything we do, we will one day give an account to God.

chapters.summary: Paul urges the Corinthians not to be puffed up but to follow his example, and reminds them that when the Lord comes he will bring to light the hidden things of the heart.
keyPoints: Paul regards himself as a servant of Christ and steward of the mysteries of God, and does not seek to be judged by man.
He warns the Corinthians not to be puffed up beyond what is written, but to follow his example.
Paul admonishes them with a father's heart, and sends Timotheus to them.
chapters.application: Let us learn Paul's humility, not judging others rashly, and not being puffed up by others' praise, seeking only the praise that comes from the Lord in the day to come.

chapters.summary: Paul rebukes the Corinthian church for tolerating sexual immorality, and calls them to put the offender out from among them, to preserve the holiness of the church.
keyPoints: A man in the church is living with his father's wife, and Paul rebukes this severely.
Paul instructs the church to deliver the offender unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh.
He stresses that the church should purge out the old leaven and keep the feast as those who are unleavened.
chapters.application: Let us set our minds on holiness, not allowing sin to grow unchecked in our lives, and with love and courage guard the purity of the church, so that Christ's name may be glorified.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers not to take one another to court before unbelievers, but to pursue holiness and glorify God.
keyPoints: Disputes between believers should be judged by wise men within the church, not brought before the courts of unbelievers.
The unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God, so believers must flee from fornication and other such sins.
The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, so we are to glorify God in our bodies.
chapters.application: When conflicts arise with fellow believers in daily life, let us humbly seek the church's help rather than taking each other to court. At the same time, let us stay watchful to keep our bodies holy, for we are the temple of the Holy Spirit.

chapters.summary: Paul responds to the Corinthian church's questions about marriage and singleness, teaching believers to serve the Lord faithfully in whatever calling they find themselves.
keyPoints: Marriage is a safeguard against fornication, and husband and wife are to give themselves to one another and not defraud each other.
Paul encourages the unmarried and widows to remain as they are, though to marry is no sin.
Believers should remain in the calling God has given them, living in a way that pleases the Lord.
chapters.application: Whether single or married, let us keep the glory of God at the center, be content and faithful in whatever situation we are in, and serve one another in love.

chapters.summary: This chapter discusses the believer's freedom and love in the matter of eating food offered to idols, stressing that knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
keyPoints: Knowledge puffs a person up, but only love builds up, so love should be the standard by which we act.
An idol is nothing at all, but our freedom must never become a stumbling block that causes a weaker brother to fall.
To sin against a brother is to sin against Christ, so we should restrain our freedom for the sake of a brother's conscience.
chapters.application: In our life of faith, let us not flaunt knowledge but show love and consideration for others. That we might not cause anyone to stumble, let us restrain our freedom and follow Christ's example of self-giving.

chapters.summary: Paul defends his apostleship, and explains that he has given up his rights and willingly serves everyone, so that he might win the more.
keyPoints: Paul proves that he is an apostle, and that he has the right to live by the gospel.
Though he has this right, he willingly gives it up for the sake of the gospel.
Like a runner in a race, he disciplines himself strictly, so that he will not be disqualified.
chapters.application: Let us follow Paul's example, willingly setting aside our own rights for the sake of the gospel, having the mind of Christ, loving others as ourselves, and practicing self-discipline in our life of faith, so that we may run well the race set before us.

chapters.summary: Paul uses the history of Israel as a warning, cautioning believers not to lust after evil things, and teaching them to do everything to the glory of God without causing anyone to stumble.
keyPoints: Though Israel's forefathers were blessed by God in the wilderness, many were overthrown because of idolatry and immorality, becoming a warning for later generations.
The temptations believers face are common to man, but God is faithful and will always provide a way of escape, so that we are able to bear it.
We cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; we must flee from idolatry and do everything for the glory of God.
themes: Temptation and the Way of Escape
chapters.application: Let us be watchful and guard ourselves, staying far from idols and sin. When temptation comes, let us trust that God will provide a way of escape, doing everything for God's glory and never causing another to stumble.

chapters.summary: Paul addresses order in the church's gatherings and at the love feast, stressing that in everything we should glorify God and examine ourselves.
keyPoints: Follow Christ, just as Paul follows Christ, and hold fast to the traditions he delivered.
He addresses the question of head coverings, stressing the order of God's creation and the authority signified because of the angels.
He rebukes the disorder at the love feast, reminding them to partake of the Lord's bread and cup in a worthy manner.
chapters.application: In the life of the church, let us respect order and treat one another in love. When we receive the Lord's Supper, let us first examine ourselves, remember the Lord's self-giving, and live out a witness of unity.

chapters.summary: Paul teaches on spiritual gifts, stressing that though the gifts are many, they come from one and the same Spirit, and that the church, like a body, needs its members to work together.
keyPoints: There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit, and the same Lord.
The church is like one body - many members, yet needing one another.
We are to earnestly desire the greater gifts, but there is a more excellent way, and that is love.
chapters.application: Each of us has different gifts. Let us serve humbly, appreciate one another, work together in the church, and display the love of Christ.

chapters.summary: This chapter sets forth the nature and eternal worth of love, stressing that love surpasses every spiritual gift and is the highest of Christian virtues.
keyPoints: Love is more excellent than any gift - without love, every ability is worth nothing.
Love includes concrete qualities such as patience, kindness, freedom from envy, and freedom from boasting.
Love never fails, while gifts such as prophecy will one day cease.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let love be our standard for action - patient and kind, slow to anger, keeping no record of wrongs - and let love become the mark of our lives.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches that in the church's gatherings we should pursue love and rightly use spiritual gifts - especially prophecy - so that the church may be built up.
keyPoints: We should pursue love, and also earnestly desire spiritual gifts - especially that we may prophesy.
Speaking in tongues without interpretation builds up only the speaker, but prophecy builds up, comforts, and encourages others.
Gatherings should be conducted properly and in order, for God is not the author of confusion, but of peace.
chapters.application: In the life of the church, let love be our foundation, let us pursue gifts that build others up, and let us keep good order in our gatherings, so that God's name may be glorified.

chapters.summary: This chapter makes clear that Christ's resurrection is the heart of the gospel, discusses the mystery of the resurrection body, and urges believers to stand firm and unmoveable.
keyPoints: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, and rose again the third day, showing the gospel to be true.
If Christ has not been raised, our faith is in vain, we are still in our sins, and we are of all men most miserable.
In the resurrection, the dead will be raised with glorious, imperishable spiritual bodies, triumphant over death, the last enemy.
chapters.application: The certainty of the resurrection assures us that our labor in this life is not in vain. Let us face each day's challenges with resurrection hope, faithfully doing the Lord's work, knowing that he will surely come again.

chapters.summary: In closing, Paul gives instructions about the collection and his travel plans, offers final exhortations, and ends the letter with greetings and a blessing.
keyPoints: He instructs them concerning the collection for the saints, that on the first day of every week each one should set aside and save something in keeping with their income.
He explains his own travel plans, along with those of Timotheus and Apollos, and urges the church to receive them well.
He exhorts the brethren to watch, stand fast in the faith, be strong, and act with love, and sends greetings to all the saints.
chapters.application: Let us give in a planned and faithful way, serve wholeheartedly, welcome fellow workers with love, stay watchful and firm in our faith, and let everything we do be done in love.
